social-networks.title: I simulated the male loneliness epidemic
social-networks.question: Isolation, algorithmic exposure, and weakening friendships can reinforce each other. I built an agent-based simulation to explore that feedback loop, then compared interventions targeting the algorithm, social support, and friendship influence.

dna-inference.title: A novel Bayesian approach to reconnecting families through DNA
dna-inference.question: Distant relatives can be difficult to distinguish from unrelated individuals using limited genetic evidence. I developed a workflow that simulates competing relationship hypotheses and estimates their support, then evaluated it across eleven pedigrees using repeated cross-validation and shuffled-label checks.

causal-inference.title: Same trainees. Different controls. Opposite conclusions.
causal-inference.question: Can observational methods recover an experimental result? I tested matching methods against a randomized job-training benchmark, then explored synthetic control in a separate application.

bayesian-housing.title: What makes an expensive home an outlier?
bayesian-housing.question: I compared three Bayesian models of Buenos Aires property prices to investigate how assumptions about unusual observations change the results.

multilevel-scores.title: No individual scores. Different bins. Still comparable?
multilevel-scores.question: All I had were score ranges and counts, and even the ranges changed between years! I built Bayesian models that worked directly with each histogram’s bin boundaries, allowing me to compare underlying score distributions without pretending I had individual records. The project uses synthetic data inspired by inconsistent reporting of test scores.

movie-preferences.title: I turned my IMDb ratings into a machine-learning experiment
movie-preferences.question: Using 615 ratings I’d collected over the years, I explored what genres, plots, and posters reveal about my movie preferences. Can a model figure out my taste?

huzur.title: Huzur: a Mongolian card game platform
huzur.question: Can an AI opponent play a traditional Mongolian card game better than I do? I’ve been playing since I was six! I built this platform to keep playing with friends after graduation took us to different countries.

forum.title: Forum: AI notes and a database for Minerva classes
forum.question: A team-built platform that turns class recordings into searchable transcripts and notes. My contribution focused on the relational database and data-integrity testing.

vinyl.title: Vinyl beyond release week
vinyl.question: National sales showed vinyl growing while CDs declined. Did individual albums tell the same story? I constructed a dataset from scattered public sales reports, compared formats at launch and later dates, and investigated the older recordings behind the market totals.

wrigley.title: Wrigley: the price of leverage
wrigley.question: A $3 billion debt-funded payout looks attractive when you count the tax shield. What happens when you count financial distress too? I combined valuation scenarios with interest-coverage constraints to assess how much debt the company could reasonably take on.

coreweave.title: An AI boom is easier to forecast than to value
coreweave.question: Our team valued CoreWeave using discounted cash flow, public comparables, and precedent transactions. The methods disagreed substantially. Why?

toyota.title: Toyota: financial policy across borders
toyota.question: How do production location, currency exposure, and financial subsidiaries change the way we interpret an automaker’s balance sheet?

aditya-birla.title: Two investments look profitable. What has to go right?
aditya-birla.question: For Aditya Birla’s proposed international investments, project profits were only part of the story. I adjusted cash flows for ownership and remittances to value what the parent company would receive, then examined how much depended on terminal value.

astral.title: A profitable investment. An uncomfortable financing problem.
astral.question: Astral Records’ equipment investment had a small positive modeled NPV and a much larger funding requirement. I examined whether the company could finance the decision.

science-technology.title: Sales up. Profits up. Where’s the cash?
science-technology.question: Science Technology planned rapid growth while improving efficiency. I connected its income forecast to receivables, inventory, and financing needs, showing why a shorter cash cycle could still leave the company needing substantially more working capital.

rvd-ai.title: Raise another million. How much of the company is left?
rvd-ai.question: I used a venture valuation model to compare how two funding amounts change the ownership bargain for RVD.AI.

optiguard.title: Same exit. Different fine print. Millions apart.
optiguard.question: Two financing structures can divide the same exit proceeds very differently. I modeled Optiguard’s capitalization and payout waterfalls to quantify how liquidation preferences and antidilution terms change what investors and founders receive.

freddo.title: Before opening another ice cream shop, follow the cash
freddo.question: A Freddo expansion analysis connecting marketing, inventory, payment terms, and working-capital requirements.
